'Comment upon the population density of fig. 6.1 (b)' names no State, no density band and no legend - the four-band choropleth of India is the entire content of the question, and the two sibling rows in the same exercise (Ex Q5(A) and Ex Q5(B)) DID get their images, so this is a missed attach rather than a chapter with no figures.

The stem is a three-part instruction whose first part is the imperative 'Explain Electric motor with the help of the following points: (i) Draw figure' - the figure is the student's deliverable, and parts (ii) principle and (iii) four appliances need nothing printed.

'Draw the diagram to show the correction of this defect' asks the student to produce the corrected ray path; set member under the shared Q4(i) context, whose parenthetical already inlines the printed figure (parallel rays converged in front of the retina), so nothing is missing on the input side.

There is no figure in this question at all - it is a pure GST word problem (AC costs Rs 51,200 with GST, CGST rate 14%) and the probe matched only on the bare `as shown in` branch inside 'find the following amounts as shown in the tax invoice of Tiptop Electronics', where 'tax invoice' is a document type the student CONSTRUCTS, not a picture on the page.

A prove-this row with no measurement to read: 'triangle QRS is an equilateral triangle' plus the arcs named in the statement give congruent chords, hence congruent arcs, hence m(arc QRS) = 240 degrees.

Angle ACB = 52 degrees is the only datum needed: the circle touching both sides of the angle at A and B gives two right angles by the tangent theorem, and the quadrilateral sum yields angle ADB = 128 degrees.

The stem IS the figure written out - 'a hand with the wrist at the right ... forefinger stretched out towards the left, thumb upwards, middle finger downwards' - which is the handedness cue that distinguishes Fleming's right hand rule from the left; the probe fired on the transcription that fixed the problem, and it carries no '[Figure: ...]' bracket so the DESCRIBED filter cannot see it.

Same pattern as Q10(a) mirrored - wrist at the left, forefinger towards the right - which is exactly what identifies Fleming's left hand rule; the description is the stem body, not a bracket, so the probe reads it as a reference.

The inlined description names every identifying feature - two cartridges with metal end caps, one glass-bodied with a thin wire visible end to end - which is enough to answer 'electric fuse' and explain its use.
'three identical units on a common base, each with a blue rocker switch marked OFF, screw terminals top and bottom' identifies a three-pole MCB without the photograph.

The description carries the two discriminating details - a SPLIT ring with brushes, and an external circuit containing an ammeter and NO cell - which is what makes the answer a DC generator rather than a motor or an AC generator.

'Complete the following diagram' is followed by a GFM pipe-table reproducing all four boxes and which two are blank, so the chart's layout and its printed entries (Morphological; Similarities in bones structure) are both carried by the row; note the PIPE_TABLE guard does not excuse it because the text also says 'diagram', which is the guard working as intended.
